rationale: Ground truth centers on two live threads: completing the validation numbers (already resolved in this diff snapshot) and whether Ref2VA was actually tested. X's review is shallow (two minor doc-indexing findings) and never touches the Ref2VA-untested risk that the diff itself flags in its 'Not yet measured' section, so it misses the substance of the ground truth almost entirely. Y extensively engages the Ref2VA-untested risk (restart command failure, OOM exposure, missing warnings) plus catches a self-contradiction in the memory-scaling formula that's directly verifiable from the diff's own numbers, and a legitimate GDDR7-vs-HBM terminology error — giving it far higher recall and actionability, with generally well-grounded (if unverifiable in places) claims.
